findings.title: A slider that lands on another Option's value leaves that Option in the Decision's "rejected" list; every later page load then says "Opening changed some details of your saved project" and keeps a needless copy
findings.description: `tune` (line 233) and `pickValues` (line 222) copy the earlier Decision's `rejected` list unchanged, and `rederive` (lines 172-180) rewrites `optionId` without touching `rejected`. So after the owner picks an Option and then moves a slider onto the value of a different Option, the Decision names that Option as current AND as rejected. The format check disagrees with the engine: `normalize` (line 724) removes the current Option from `rejected` on opening. The saved text and the opened project therefore differ, and the Studio's `changedOnOpening` (apps/studio/src/store.ts lines 147-149, used at line 419) reports a change that nobody made. Broken invariants: (1) `rejected` never contains `optionId`; (2) a project the engine produced opens with no change and no note. A second path gives the same state: a hand-set second color, then a main-color change that makes the hand-set value equal a following Option.
findings.failure_scenario: Step "Corner rounding": pick "Soft" (14), open "Adjust with sliders", press Left six times (value 8 = the Option "subtle"). Saved Decision: kind tuned, optionId "subtle", rejected [square, crisp, subtle, pill]. Reload the page: a banner says "Opening changed some details of your saved project. The Studio kept the copy as it was; you can download it from the Summary." and one kept copy appears. The banner returns on every reload until the owner changes the project again. The same happens with border weight (pick "medium", two presses "thinner"), density, contrast, and others, because many Option values lie on the slider grids.
findings.evidence: Property run (600 random sequences, 9,362 actions, sliders moved the way the Studio moves them): "V2 rejected contains the current Option: 158 times" and "V7 reload changes the project: 158 times"; no other invariant broke. Real Studio in Chromium (browser.cjs, lines S1): after the steps above the stored Decision was {"kind":"tuned","rejected":["square","crisp","subtle","pill"],...,"optionId":"subtle","values":{"radius":8}}; reload 1, 2 and 3 each printed banners ["Opening changed some details of your saved project. The Studio kept the copy as it was; you can download it from the Summary."] and kept copies ["Your saved copy as it was, before the Studio changed details on opening it."]. Mutation check: removing `&& id !== optionId` from normalize (line 724) leaves all 97 unit tests green, and the existing 400-sequence sweep never hits the case because it tunes to random real numbers that never equal an Option.

findings.title: A second color that was never set to follow the main color starts to follow it after the main color passes one particular hue (path-dependent design; a "kept" Decision is rewritten)
findings.description: `rederive` decides whether the second color follows the main color by asking whether the design matched a following Option before the change (line 163). A fixed second color can match such an Option by coincidence for one hue of the main color. From that moment the engine treats the second color as following, although neither the Direction nor the owner chose that. The result depends on the order and even on the input device: a keyboard walk of the hue slider hits every whole number, a quick mouse drag may jump over the hue. Two curated Directions carry a fixed second color ("Galactic Goth" 302/18 and "Frontier Gazette" 38/245). For Galactic Goth the coincidence hue 258 is the Option "ink-blue", so two ordinary clicks reach it. Afterward "Put this Step back" on the main-color Step does not restore the Direction's second color, and a Decision of kind "kept" on the color Step is silently rewritten to a different Option and value.

The second color is now 315 (a pink), not 18 (the Direction's red). Picking "teal" directly leaves it at 18. With "Frontier Gazette": press Right on the main-color hue slider from 38 to 70; from 66 on the second color moves (246, 247, ... 250). One drag straight to 70 leaves it at 245. Then "Put this Step back" gives main 38 and second 218, not the Direction's 245.

findings.title: A slider key press that cannot move the value still rewrites the Decision; at the top of the "Corner rounding" slider it replaces "Pill" (999) with 28
findings.description: The key handler calls `s.tuneValue(t.key, nextSliderValue(t, Math.min(value, t.max), steps))` for every slider key, and `tuneValue` (apps/studio/src/store.ts line 616) commits `tune(...)` without checking whether anything changes. `tune` (engine.ts lines 226-234) always writes a Decision of kind "tuned" with a new time. Two effects. (1) At an end of a slider a key press changes no value but turns "Picked" or "Kept" into "Set by hand" and adds an Undo entry. (2) With "Pill" (radius 999, above the slider's top of 28) the key for "rounder" (Right, Up, Page Up, End) sets the radius to 28. That changes the page in the opposite sense for controls: `--radius-control` 999px to 28px, `--radius-small` 999px to 14px, `--radius-surface` 28px to 42px. `nextSliderValue` (engine.ts lines 248-254) has no rule for a value outside the slider's range.
findings.failure_scenario: (1) Pick "Square" on "Corner rounding", open the sliders, press Left: the radius stays 0, the Decision changes from picked to tuned. (2) Pick "Pill", open the sliders (the text says "fully round", the knob stands at the right end), press Right: the radius becomes 28, the text says "28px", the card on show becomes "Your design now", and the Decision is hand-set with no Option.
findings.evidence: Real Studio in Chromium (browser2.cjs line N1): "after picking Square: radius 0 Decision picked square 2026-11-13T21:33:20.771Z" then "after ArrowLeft on the slider at its left end: radius 0 Decision tuned square 2026-11-13T21:33:23.156Z | Undo button enabled: true". (browser.cjs lines S2): "after picking Pill: radius 999 Decision kind picked pill | slider text: fully round | slider knob value: 28" then "after ArrowRight ('rounder') on the slider at its right end: radius 28 Decision {kind:tuned, optionId:null, values:{radius:28}} | slider text: 28px | checked card: option-current". Unit run (D.txt): "tokens changed: --radius-control: 999px -> 28px, --radius-surface: 28px -> 42px, --radius-small: 999px -> 14px".
findings.suggested_fix: In `nextSliderValue`, return `current` unchanged when the key points past the end the value already stands at or beyond (`steps > 0 && current >= tunable.max`, `steps < 0 && current <= tunable.min`); pass the real value (not `Math.min(value, t.max)`) from the key handler; and in `tuneValue` do nothing when the new value equals the current one. Add unit cases for 999 with +1 and for a key press at each end.

findings.title: A project file with a corner radius between 29 and 998 is accepted, drawn with corner tokens up to 1,498 px, and described on screen as "fully round"
findings.description: The format check accepts any radius from 0 to 999 (packages/core/src/params.ts line 110). The token derivation treats only 999 or more as "Pill" (tokens.ts lines 559-564) and multiplies every other value: `--radius-surface` is 1.5 times the radius. The Studio's slider text says "fully round" for any radius above 28 (apps/studio/src/App.tsx line 60). So a value that no Option, no Direction and no slider can produce passes the check, is drawn with tokens that differ from the real Pill (which uses 28px for boxes), and is labelled as if it were the Pill. Reaching this needs a hand-edited or foreign file.
findings.failure_scenario: Open a project file whose `params.radius` is 500. The Studio accepts it without a note. Tokens: --radius-control 500px, --radius-surface 750px, --radius-small 250px (the Pill gives 999px, 28px, 999px). The slider text reads "fully round".

App.tsx line 60: `if (t.key === 'radius' && raw > t.max) return 'fully round';`.

findings.title: Test gaps: six changes to the engine leave all 97 unit tests green
findings.description: I ran a mutation sweep on a scratch copy of packages/core (engine.test.ts, project-file.test.ts, catalog.test.ts; 97 tests; 19 mutants; 13 killed). These six survived. (1) `normalize` no longer removes the current Option from `rejected` (engine.ts line 724): this is the gap behind the first finding. (2) Options with an overused-look warning are weighted like any other when Directions are generated (line 511, `o.warn ? 0.12 : 1`): the comment's promise "chosen rarely" has no test. (3) Generated Direction ids ignore the seed (line 557): two batches from "more Directions" would share ids such as generated-0-0, and the Studio finds a generated Direction's name by id; the unit test checks ids only inside one batch. (4) `designDistance` without the wrap at 0/360 (line 461): hues 350 and 10 would count as 340 degrees apart. (5) `activeTunables` returns every slider (line 310, the U3-06 fix): no unit test; `closerOptions` depends on it. A browser test may cover the slider itself; I did not run the browser tests. (6) `closerOptions` returns up to 8 variations in place of 6 (line 353). Also, the existing 400-sequence sweep (line 351) tunes to random real numbers, so it never lands on an Option value or on a slider grid point the way the Studio does.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit that breaks any of these six behaviors passes `npm test` unnoticed. For (3) the visible result would be that two batches of generated Directions share ids, so the Summary can name the wrong generated Direction.
findings.evidence: Output of mutate.py: "baseline: all tests pass :: Tests 97 passed (97)"; "M1 normalize keeps the current Option in rejected: SURVIVED"; "M3 warned Options weighted like any other in generated Directions: SURVIVED"; "M7 designDistance without hue wrap: SURVIVED"; "M29 activeTunables returns every slider: SURVIVED"; "M42 closerOptions returns up to 8: SURVIVED"; "M43 generated Direction ids ignore the seed: SURVIVED". Killed, for comparison: the clamps in tune and nextSliderValue, the conflict filter in generateDirections, three harmony or conflict rules, the text and list limits of the format check, the time check, the F-3 note, and revert.

findings.title: deriveTokens repeats the same gamut search hundreds of times: 1,346 color conversions for a 26-color palette; two small caches cut its time by 54 to 63 percent
findings.description: toGamut (lines 53-63) runs a 24-step search whenever a color is outside what screens can show, and nothing remembers the result. toRgb, luminance, emittedRgb, writtenContrast and contrastOverEmitted each call it again for the same color object. The commonest colors are outside: the plain start's page background (lightness 0.985, chroma 0.012, hue 255 gives a blue channel of 1.03) and the near-white label that readableOn tries first (lightness 0.99, chroma 0.005). So each use of the page background costs 26 conversions instead of 2. On top of that, basePalette calls readableOn(accent) four to five times with the same input (tokens.ts lines 126, 143, 164, 165), and deriveTokens converts every palette color twice (tokens.ts lines 579-580: toCss and toHex are the same function).

findings.evidence: Vitest, counting Math.cos calls (one per conversion): deriveTokens(DEFAULT_PARAMS): off 1,346, advise 1,636, enforce 1,926 conversions; random designs under enforce: mean 3,146, most 13,918. findings.repro: In a vitest file under packages/core/test: const cos = Math.cos; let n = 0; Math.cos = (x) => { n++; return cos(x); }; deriveTokens(DEFAULT_PARAMS, 'off'); Math.cos = cos; n is 1346. findings.description: init() registers the pagehide and visibilitychange listeners (store.ts:518, 526-528) and the top bar's name field is live (App.tsx:167, 931) BEFORE `openSaved(await loadSaved())` (store.ts:534) has finished. The window is as long as the page database takes to answer (the code allows up to 10 s for `use('db')` plus 10 s for `get()`). Without a page database the read finishes inside one task, so this needs the private page (or any host with `window.claude`). If the page database holds the work, the next visit opens the EMPTY project and demotes the real work to a kept copy ("The older of two saved copies that differed"). findings.title: A page runtime whose use() is missing or throws makes the Studio ignore the saved browser copy and then overwrite it
findings.description: database() calls `rt.use('db').catch(...)` with no guard. If `window.claude` exists but `use` is absent, throws at once, or returns something that is not a promise, database() throws. readPage() awaits it outside its try block (platform.ts:95), so loadSaved() rejects AFTER readBrowser() already read the browser copy and set `browserSavedAtSeen`. init()'s catch (store.ts:535-537) then shows "The Studio could not look for a saved project. It started a new one." and leaves saving switched on. The first edit writes the new empty project over the saved browser copy (no conflict, no kept copy). saveProject() then awaits database() again (platform.ts:259), which throws, so saveNow() rejects unhandled and the status line stays at "Saving…" for good. The same fail-open applies to any other exception between loadSaved() and the end of openSaved(). I could not check whether the real private page can produce such a runtime; if it can, this is a loss of saved work. I graded it medium because that trigger is unverified.
findings.failure_scenario: `window.claude = {}` (or `{ use() { throw new Error('capability not declared') } }`); browser copy "Weeks of work" (Soft Daylight, 1 Decision). Open the Studio: the name field shows "My first project". Type one change into the name field.
findings.evidence: c2.cjs printed: `C[no-use] 1 opened: status "Nothing to save yet", nameOnScreen "My first project", notice ["The Studio could not look for a saved project. It started a new one."], stored {name:"Weeks of work",…}` then `C[no-use] 2 after one edit + 2.5 s: status "Saving…", stored {name:"One edit",direction:null,decisions:0}, kept [], errors ["TypeError: e.use is not a function"]`. The `use-throws` shape gave the same result with `errors ["Error: capability not declared"]`.
findings.suggested_fix: In database(), call the runtime inside a promise chain, for example `Promise.resolve().then(() => rt.use('db')).catch(() => null)`, so that a throw or a non-promise becomes `null` ("no page database"). In init()'s catch, do not leave saving on over a copy that was never opened: set `saved: 'held'` with a hold notice, or open the browser copy that readBrowser() already returned.

findings.title: After a first read of the page database fails, the second read lets the next save replace the page copy without keeping it
findings.description: When the first read times out or rejects (readPage's catch returns 'timeout', platform.ts:104-106), openSaved() starts retryPageRead(). A successful second read sets `pageReadSucceeded = true` (platform.ts:100), so the next save writes to the page database. The retry handler (store.ts:478-488) keeps nothing: an unreadable page copy returns silently (`!result.ok`), an older copy that differs returns silently (`!pageIsNewer`), and a newer copy only raises a hold notice that does not stop saving. "Keep what I have" drops the newer copy without keeping it, and "Open the newer copy" calls replaceProject() directly, so the project on screen is not kept either (Undo only). A normal open keeps the same copies ("The older of two saved copies that differed", "A saved copy that could not be read"). This breaks rule 2 in the header of platform.ts ("A copy that cannot be read is never overwritten") and guarantee 10.05 (keeps a copy before work is replaced). The newer-page-copy case is the owner who worked on another computer.
findings.failure_scenario: Stand-in whose first `get()` rejects and whose second answers. (D1) Page copy "Newer on page" (2026-11-13), browser copy "Browser older" (2026-11-06): the hold "A newer copy of this project was found saved on this page." appears; press "Keep what I have", change the name once: the page copy is replaced, kept copies: none. (D1b) Do not answer, change the name once: the page copy is replaced while the notice still offers it. (D2) Unreadable page copy: no notice at all; one edit replaces it; nothing kept. (D3) Older page copy that differs: no notice; replaced; nothing kept.

Make "Open the newer copy" go through replaceKeepingCopy(). Add browser tests with a stand-in whose first read fails.

If one `set()` never settles, saveNow() (store.ts:293) never returns: `lastSavedText` and `lastOutcome` are not updated and `saved` stays 'saving'. Every later save queues behind the stuck promise, so the page database is not even asked again, even if it recovers. The browser copy is written each time, so nothing is lost on this computer, but the status line never says so and the page copy stays old.

findings.title: On the Summary, every keystroke and every Undo re-reads the whole kept-copies list twice and redraws every row; the cost grows with the number of kept copies

Note: 1,000 full copies cannot exist: a project with all 23 Decisions is 6,778 characters (7,821 as a list member), so 1,000 need 7.8 million characters and the browser refused the write (QuotaExceededError); about 660 fit. I therefore measured 200 and 600 full copies, and 1,000 copies of the smallest project the Studio keeps (Direction only, 3,256 characters).
findings.failure_scenario: Kept-copies list with 200 / 600 full copies or 1,000 small copies; on the Summary, type one character into the project-name field, or press Undo.

For comparison, on the Steps screen a keystroke costs 11-16 ms and an Undo 8-10 ms at 0, 200, 600 and 1,000 copies, with 0 list reads. Per keystroke on every screen: the whole project is turned into JSON text 3 times (all in the delayed save: saveNow twice, openEnvelope once; under 0.5 ms together), 4 times on the Summary; 2 JSON.parse calls; 1 getItem and 1 setItem of the project key. findings.title: A slider step costs 61 to 92 ms of main-thread work; a held key or a drag keeps the main thread busy without a break
findings.description: Every slider step changes project.params, so `stateKey` (line 431) changes and the `thumbs` memo (lines 432-436) builds the Mockup document again for EVERY card of the Step, although only one card ("Your design now") shows a different design. Each build runs deriveTokens plus renderSmallBusiness and makes a string of 68,000 to 100,000 characters (two fonts travel inside each document), which useFrameKey then compares with the old string. On a color Step, `Swatches` (lines 314-316, used at line 589) derives the tokens of every card a second time. Two preview documents are then re-created per step (the large preview and the "Your design now" card): those two are necessary, because the design changed and a locked frame cannot be updated in place. findings.title: Slider keys change a "fully round" design to 28 px, record steps that change nothing, and swallow Alt+Arrow
findings.description: The key handler of a slider (lines 634-640) calls s.tuneValue for every key in SLIDER_KEYS without asking whether the value would change, and without looking at modifier keys. It works from Math.min(value, t.max). Three things go wrong. (a) Corner rounding has a value above the slider's top ("fully round"). ArrowRight, PageUp or End, which mean "rounder", compute 28 and write it, so the design gets LESS round and the Decision changes from "Picked: Fully round" to "Set by hand". (b) A key press at the end of any slider (ArrowLeft at the low end, End at the top) changes nothing, yet tune() in the core always returns a new project (engine.ts:226-234), so each press adds an Undo step and, on an undecided Step, would record a Decision. Undo then reports a change that did not happen. (c) Alt+ArrowLeft, the browser's "Back" shortcut on Windows and Linux, is cancelled and moves the slider instead.

(b) On "Line thickness" press Home, then ArrowLeft three times, then Undo once. (c) Focus a slider and press Alt+ArrowLeft.

C2 after 3 x ArrowLeft at the low end {"out":"0px"}; C2 after one Undo {"out":"0px","rail":"Set by hand, No dividing lines","notice":["Undone: the Step “Line thickness” is back to how it was."]} (nothing came back; the notice says it did). check2.cjs printed: C11 Alt+ArrowLeft on the slider: default prevented true value 1.1 -> 1.05. The existing browser test (studio.e2e.ts, about line 962-980) presses ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, End and Home on "Spacing" only; it never presses a key at an end or on a value above the top, so this mutation survives.

As a second guard, let tuneValue in store.ts (line 616) return when the clamped value equals project.params[key]. Add browser tests for both cases.

A move to another Step through the address (the browser's Back and Forward buttons) runs the effect at line 386, which replaces the typed text with the stored one. On the Steps screen the body is a place where Enter means "pick and continue" (line 457).

findings.title: The question "Yes, remove it for good / No, keep it" disappears when the save status changes
findings.description: `removing` holds the KeptCopy object itself (line 691) and the row compares by identity (`removing === copy`, line 761). `keptCopies` is read again from storage whenever s.notice or s.saved changes (line 693), which makes new objects, so the comparison fails and the row falls back to "Remove this kept copy…". A save that finishes 300 ms after any edit is enough. The same memo also reads and parses every kept copy twice per keystroke in the name field on the Summary (once for "Saving…", once for the result).
findings.failure_scenario: On the Summary, press "Remove this kept copy…"; before answering, type one letter into the project name (or have pressed the button within 0.3 s of an edit). The two answer buttons vanish and the first button is back.

findings.suggested_fix: Remember the copy by a stable key (for example `${copy.keptAt}|${copy.text.length}|${index}`) and compare keys; and re-read the list only on keptTick and on s.notice, not on every change of s.saved.

Give each notice a running number in the store and use it as the key of the

in the row, so that a repeated notice replaces the paragraph and is announced again.

findings.title: The color chips of every card are worked out again on every render of a color Step, also for each letter typed into the project name
findings.description: StepsView subscribes to the whole store (`useStudio()`, line 398), so it renders again on every change, including rename. For the six color Steps, each card renders `Swatches` (line 589), which calls deriveTokens (line 315) with no memo. The previews themselves are safe: project.name is not part of `stateKey`, and no preview document is re-created while typing.
findings.failure_scenario: On "Main color" (14 cards) type a project name. Each letter costs about 9 ms of extra script for 14 token derivations whose result is thrown away unchanged.
findings.evidence: perf2.cjs, 20 letters typed one by one, mean per letter: Steps screen "Main color" 43.8 ms main-thread, 12.9 ms script; Steps screen "First screen" (4 cards, no chips) 23.6 ms, 3.8 ms script; Directions 16.7 ms, 2.9 ms script; Summary 35.2 ms, 3.8 ms script. All values stay under 50 ms per letter on this machine.

findings.title: A reason typed on one Step is stored on a different Step when the browser's Back or Forward button changes the Step; it replaces that Step's own reason
findings.description: The field "Why this choice?" (ReasonField, App.tsx lines 382-395) is one component for all Steps: line 621 mounts it without a key, so the same input element stays in place when the Step changes. The field stores its text only when it loses keyboard focus (onBlur, line 391), and the store's setReason (apps/studio/src/store.ts line 623) writes to whichever Step is current at that moment, not to the Step the text was typed for. When the Step changes while the field still has focus (browser Back or Forward button, a mouse's back button, Alt+Left, a swipe), the Studio first makes the new Step current and then moves focus to the cards (App.tsx lines 467-469). The field loses focus, and its handler saves the text of the old Step onto the Decision of the new Step. The new Step's own reason is replaced, the Step where the owner typed keeps no reason, no notice appears, and the status line says "Saved". Undo brings the replaced reason back, but nothing tells the owner to use it. The screen reviewer reported that the Back button loses a typed reason; this is a different result: the text lands on the wrong Decision. I rank it medium, not high, because it touches one optional line of text and Undo can restore it. No browser test types into this field (0 mentions of the field in apps/studio/e2e/studio.e2e.ts).
findings.failure_scenario: Start from the first Direction. Press the main button on Step 1 "Menu (navigation)" and on Step 2 "First screen" (both now have a Decision). Go back to Step 1, type "my reason for the first Step" and click elsewhere (stored). Go forward to Step 2, click into "Why this choice?", type "typed on Step 2", and press the browser's Back button without leaving the field. Result in storage: the Decision of Step 1 (nav) has reason "typed on Step 2" (its own reason is gone); the Decision of Step 2 (hero) has no reason. The Forward button does the same in the other direction.
findings.evidence: Output of reason.cjs (Chromium, built page local-test.html).
